read.sections.0.text.note: Crops: millet (China) is ข้าวฟ่างหางกระรอก (foxtail millet) and sorghum (Africa) is ข้าวฟ่าง; maize ข้าวโพด, taro เผือก, barley ข้าวบาร์เลย์. In the picture China says ข้าว ข้าวฟ่าง and Africa ข้าวฟ่างหลายชนิด to fit. Check the crop names.
read.sections.0.text.source: For most of human history, people got their food by foraging. They gathered wild plants, hunted animals and caught fish. More than 10,000 years ago, some groups began to plant seeds and keep animals. Farming did not start in just one place or at one time, and different parts of the world grew different crops. Farmers in West Asia grew wheat and barley, while farmers in China grew rice and millet. People in New Guinea grew bananas and taro, and people in Mexico grew maize and beans. People in the Andes mountains first farmed potatoes, and people in parts of Africa first farmed sorghum. In Harapan Valley, one group still moves around to find food, while the other group farms.
read.sections.0.text.back: For almost all of human history, people got food by foraging. They gathered wild plants, hunted animals and caught fish. More than 10,000 years ago, some groups began growing plants and keeping animals. Farming didn't begin in one place or at one time, and each part of the world grew different crops. Farmers in West Asia grew wheat and barley, while farmers in China grew rice and foxtail millet. People in New Guinea grew bananas and taro, and people in Mexico grew maize and beans. People in the Andes mountains were the first to grow potatoes, and people in parts of Africa were the first to grow sorghum. In Harapan Valley, one group still keeps moving to find food, while another group farms.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: Long ago, people got food by foraging. They picked wild plants and caught fish. More than 10,000 years ago, some groups began to farm. They planted seeds and kept animals. Farming began in many places at different times. Each place had its own crops. West Asia grew wheat, and China grew rice. Mexico grew corn. Parts of Africa grew other grains. In Harapan Valley, one group moves to find food. The other group farms.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: Long ago, people got food by foraging. They gathered wild plants and caught fish. More than 10,000 years ago, some groups began farming. They grew plants and kept animals. Farming began in many places, at different times. Each place had its own crops. West Asia grew wheat. China grew rice. Mexico grew maize. Parts of Africa grew other kinds of grain. In Harapan Valley, one group moves to find food. Another group farms.

read.sections.1.heading.source: Extra food changed work and trade

read.sections.1.text.source: Farming could grow a lot of food in a small area. After a good harvest, a village might have a surplus, which is more food than people need right away. With extra grain in store, not everyone had to farm, so some people could specialise in making pots, cloth or tools. In Harapan Valley, one family makes clay pots and gives them to farmers in exchange for grain. This is a kind of trade. Villages also traded with each other, and a village near the sea might trade salt for grain. Over time, some farming villages grew into towns.
read.sections.1.text.back: Farming grows a lot of food on a small area. After a good harvest, a village might have a surplus, which is more food than people need at the time. With grain kept in a store, not everyone has to farm, so some people can specialise, such as making pots, weaving cloth or making tools. In Harapan Valley, one family makes clay pots and swaps them with farmers for grain. This is one kind of trade. Villages also trade with each other: a village near the sea might trade salt for grain. Over time, some farming villages grew into towns.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: A farm can grow lots of food in a small space. After a good year, there may be a surplus of extra food. People keep it safe for later. Now not everyone has to farm, so some people can specialise. They do one main job, like making pots. In Harapan Valley, one family makes pots. They give pots and get grain. This is trade. Villages trade with each other too, and some grow into towns.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: Farms grow a lot of food on a small area. After a good year, there may be a surplus. People keep it for later. Now not everyone has to farm. So some people can specialise. They do mainly one job, such as making pots. In Harapan Valley, one family makes pots. They give pots and get grain back. This is trade. Villages trade with each other too, and some villages grow into towns.

read.sections.2.text.source: Farming was hard work, with long days of planting, watering and harvesting. Many villages depended on only a few crops. If the rain did not come, the harvest could fail and people had little to eat. Living close to animals and to many other people also helped some illnesses spread. In some places, a few families took control of more land and stored grain, which gave them more power. Not every group chose to farm, and many kept foraging or did some of both. So historians ask a careful question: was farming better, and better for whom?
read.sections.2.text.back: Farming is hard work; planting, watering and harvesting take all day. Many villages depended on only a few crops. If the rain didn't come, the harvest could fail and people had little to eat. Living close to animals and to many people also made some diseases spread more easily. In some places, a few families came to control more of the land and the stored grain, which gave them more power. Not every group chose to farm. Many groups kept foraging, or did both. So historians ask carefully: was farming really better, and better for whom?

read.sections.2.simpler.source: Farming is hard work. Many villages grow only a few crops. If no rain comes, the crops can die. Then there is not much to eat. People live close to animals and to each other, so sickness can spread. Some families get more land and food. This gives them more power. Not every group chooses to farm. Many keep foraging. So we ask: was farming better? Who was it better for?
read.sections.2.simpler.back: Farming is hard work. Many villages grew only a few crops. If the rain doesn't come, the crops may die. Then there isn't much to eat. People lived close to animals and close to each other, so diseases could spread. Some families got more land and food. This gave them more power. Not every group chose to farm. Many groups kept foraging. So we ask: was farming better? Better for whom?

write.example.source: Farming helped people because it could grow a lot of food in one place. One example from the lesson is the farming village in Harapan Valley. After a good harvest, it has a surplus of grain. This lets one family specialise in making pots. But farming also brought a problem: the village grows only a few crops. watch.summary.source: This video explains why farming was such a big change in human history. For a very long time, people found their food in the wild. Then people in several parts of the world began to grow crops and keep animals. Farming could make more food in a smaller area. So more people could live in one place, and villages could grow. Stored food let some people do other work, like making tools or trading. Some people became leaders. Farming also changed the land around people. But farming brought risks too. A bad harvest could mean hunger. Illness could spread more easily. Some people got much more land and power than others. Farming was very important, but it did not make life better for everyone in the same way.
watch.summary.back: This video explains why farming was a huge change in human history. For a very long time people found food in nature. Then people in many parts of the world began growing crops and keeping animals. Farming produced more food on less land, so more people could live in one place and villages grew. Stored food let some people do other work, such as making tools or trading. Some people became leaders. Farming also changed the land around people. But farming brought risks too. A failed harvest could mean hunger. Diseases spread more easily. Some people got far more land and power than others. Farming was very important, but it didn't make everyone's life better in the same way.

educatorNotes.1.source: Dates are rounded on purpose ('more than 10,000 years ago'). Farming began at different times in different regions; avoid presenting one region as first or best, or foragers as 'behind'.
